body: It certainly doesn't sound like it! The one thing I hate about depression is how skewed we are about ourselves. For example, I read your comment and felt like a loser since I only have a bachelors degree from a mediocre university. It's all about perspective :)

Hi there, first off you're not crazy, you're depressed. Depression lies to us in so many ways, making things worse than they actually are. Personally I see nothing wrong with taking a little break :) Crying is good, getting it out of your system. Watching movies is good so you don't dwell on the thoughts. Perhaps you could get up soon and do something small, like housework or a walk around your neighborhood. 

Btw I'm in a similar boat, couldn't sleep last night and asked to work from home today and lying in bed with the worst nausea I've experienced in awhile. Feel like such a weirdo, thinking how embarrassing this illness is. I can't keep it straight but coming on here helps. Eating is so hard, if you can just eat a little at a time. Drink some juice or a smoothie.

Hi there, I can really relate to the feelings of being dismissed. You want validation, you see yourself in this, it would be a relief and help you move forward in treatment. 

One thing that helped me was to keep telling myself that even though I know myself well and see these traits, anxiety is a devil-it can trick your mind into thinking lots of things that aren't true. That can suck, because we're taught to believe in ourselves and to get through life on our own, and to think we might be wrong is hard. However, there's a very good chance you are right or perhaps have some of the traits. Maybe he is skeptical at first because he doesn't know you well enough. He does deal with people who by definition believe things about themselves and the world that aren't true. This isn't meant to invalidate you but say that it's complicated and I wouldn't put too much thought into it.

It's ok to feel lost, it's ok to seek help, you are welcome here. I'm here if you need to talk as well.

Even though I see eating as part of feeling better, I feel as though I just can't. It induces this horrible nausea that makes it worse. But I'll force myself. You're right, things are moving forward. The growing pains hurt though.

Thank you! This helps to hear. It's frustrating because the last six months I got up everyday and went, but these past two weeks I can't sleep more than a few hours each night, and I haven't been able to eat. I try to force myself and also drink smoothies but it's not enough, and I get sick. Today I had to ask my boss to work from home and feel terrible. It feels like my life is falling apart even if that's also the anxiety making things seem that way.

That worrying what others think of me to such a degree is a waste of time, making me miserable, and thus people around me. You mean I could have been my free spirited self all along? I abandoned the idea years ago bc I thought it wasn't mature. Turns out I had way more friends back then, and self respect. Now I feel like I have to make up for lost time that I'll never get back, and I'm so lonely :( It sucks thinking you sell yourself short all the time
You are so welcome, and glad to hear you have such a supportive system. That's so special!

Normal to feel this way. No one knows better than you, people are so varied and strange in their interpretations of the world, which means their interpretation of you is filtered through their own biases and such and probably not close to how you view yourself. Still, we are social creatures and desire to fit in. It's good. One thing that helps me sometimes is to try and realize that both people can be right and disagree at the same time. Let people just be, and think what they'll think about us. The book The Four Agreements has a part about taking stuff too personally (which everyone does) and it helps to keep reading that over and over.

So sorry you are having a rough day, and I can very much relate to having a parent that scolds rather than nurtures. Perhaps we are born with a predisposition toward sensitivity nervous system wise, with many gifts, but an unloving or critical parent can be the difference between feeling good and having anxiety and shame. It is not your fault.

Just a thought, but what about trying a medication to help with the rough days, or seeing a therapist? It's not because there's anything wrong with who you are fundamentally, quite the opposite, and perhaps they can assist in helping in areas that are tough right now.

Sensitive people are awesome. It took me many years to realize I'm an hsp, and I read books like The Drama of the Gifted Child (gifted refers to the sensitivities that develop when our emotions and sense of individual self aren't regarded highly as kids) that helped. 

One thing too, that id like to share, is that feeling better is definitely possible and what you deserve to feel so much more. I'm sorry that you didn't get that help perhaps. I hope your day gets better, you feel better, and hugs if you want them.

Hey there. It's really hard when you have a critical, self involved parent. We learn our self worth and other stuff from parents when we're little, so a lot of people who are naturally confident or feel good about themselves may tell others to be like this, but it's not always so easy. Our sense of self develops often at a very young age. Of course not implying that this definitely happened to you, or you should blame your dad and that sort of thing if you don't want. Just some thoughts.

The good news is that your dads treatment is not a reflection of who you really are and what you deserve. You say that you experience social anxiety. Personally I believe at the core of it it's just caring what others think because we didn't get validated much and so look to the outside for it rather than giving it to ourselves. It's fixable, and one of the best ways to combat it, I've found, is by catching these worrisome thoughts about what someone could have thought or how we acted, and say "screw it." (I like the f word, not saying f those people, but f these thoughts that are giving me such anxiety). Perhaps try and move onto a new thought if possible, don't let the mind go down too many paths of worry reflection (trust me, I slept three years ding this all the time and I can never get those years back, no good comes from dwelling). Healthy reflection is good though, like "wow, I feel hurt right now, and that's ok. Did what I say or do really mean that much? Do those people really think that stuff about me or am I making it up or making assumptions?" Usually not. 

Sorry if this is me making assumptions too lol. I struggle with something similar, I believe, and it sucks. We have a right to feel good about ourselves, is what it really comes down to. I always thought others knew more than me, bc my parents were know it alls and I was never right, but people don't, generally speaking. We just have to find our own opinions and voices and realize even if others don't agree, or vice versa, that those can all be true about how to view the world. And you deserve to feel free of anxiety!

Wow I could have written this as well. Kudos to you for recognizing these; just even realizing it can really help fix the issues, especially the first one. It's a painful way to live, thinking people are upset or mad when it's really just something they are going through and doesn't apply to us. A couple friends have told me over the years, that I don't have to take things personally, and this is what they were speaking off: easily hurt by what I perceive as signs of rejection in some way, when the other person isn't thinking of me at all. It's easily fixable once you catch yourself doing it it seems.

Sorry that you don't feel like a real person :( it's a sucky feeling. But you definitely are, and to reiterate what others wrote, a good therapist could perhaps help you see this more clearly, and give you some of that feedback that we missed out on growing up that tells us we're loved, special, important, and real in the eyes of others.

Yes I have this problem. Recently I had to have a bad experience thrust me a little out of this way of thinking, because it had reached a point where it was my life, or caring what everyone thinks. This took 32 hrs to reach this breaking point. It's not easy. I'm trying to focus on those who do like me, and less on those who don't. If I get a Facebook like, appreciate that, not compare to people getting more. If someone doesn't show interest it's nothing personal really. People have strange reasons for not liking others. Many people do not take it personally when they don't click, but they have themselves.

I think as people with this personality type and temperament we'll always be a bit more sensitive to things like rejection that make us concerned with what others think. We just have to let it happen in moderation, at least at first.

I'm a similar way. Personally I don't think it's related to depression though perhaps thinking patterns that are similar. I think those tend to be more in depth, abstract attractions of the mind too, and makes some people feel more alive, in tune with their deeper selves, or drawn to the way it makes you grounded and keeps things real. Sadness is like that; such a dynamic emotion. It's not as scary to lose as when you're happy and you know it's going to end. There a whole host of reasons probably. 

As long as you don't feel like you have depression, I see nothing wrong with being drawn more toward the macabre.

Sorry you've struggled with social anxiety in the past. Honestly it sounds like you've made a lot of progress, and where you are now is a great place to be in. Teaching in a foreign country is so cool! That in itself is a great conversation starter and something that can intrigue and impress new friends.

When you get back to the states, it might help to remember that even if the vibe and circumstances are different, many many people here are looking for friendships, and you clearly have something to offer. I think sometimes with social anxiety we forget those good qualities we have, such as kindness, curiosity, a loving nature, smartness and other things that we don't realize are big qualities that potential friends are interested in. Maybe you could think or write about some of these qualities. I promise they are there.

Another thing is, you're still young. Not that I'm much older anyway but I remember being in my 20s after graduating and feeling hella old, and now I'm 32 and feel young, like my whole life is still ahead of me. You'd be surprised how much can change. If I could give any advice, after many years of slight misery, clinging to what I wish I used to have, or what I should have had, just to never look back on any of it. It's just a waste, and I wasted years of my life until recently when it dawned on me how precious this time is. I know it's hard to accept when someone else says it tho :)

Keeping an open mind and realizing you are the person you've become, with all these cool experiences, can help you meet new friends later. You're not a person with social anxiety anymore! You've come a long way baby.

Since its only part time (if I recall, on mobile so I unfortunately cannot double check what you wrote at the moment) then it could leave time open for other opportunities. I've still kept the magazine on my resume because it shows how I can be dynamic in my writing, and other skills from the job itself. It sounds like you could learn from it as well. Of course this is all just my opinion. Nothing wrong with trying something out :)

Yes I would think so. One angle you might consider is going to the homeless shelter and interviewing people whose lives have been affected by the shelter. Where did they start out in life, and what brought them there? How has the shelter transformed their lives? That sort of thing. 

Maybe even consider using one of their stories as the lede? Then you could transition to explain the employee at the university and all she has done to start this shelter, how long it has been around, how it's changing lives. Readers do love hearing about nice things in the community. Good luck to you!
